facts.text: Ipanema beach gained worldwide fame when Antônio Carlos Jobim and Vinícius de Moraes wrote "The Girl from Ipanema" in the 1960s.
The neighborhood was founded in 1894 by José Antônio Moreira, later known as the Ipanema Count, who established the first urban settlement.
Ipanema’s name comes from Tupi words meaning "stinking pond," reflecting its original river in São Paulo.
Every Sunday, the street closest to the beach closes to cars, letting locals and tourists skate, bike, or stroll along the ocean.
The Dois Irmãos mountains rise at the western end of the beach, creating a dramatic backdrop for surfers and sunbathers.
During Brazil’s military dictatorship, Ipanema became a refuge for artists and musicians seeking freedom, drawing crowds from across the country.
